open_points.subject: Create replay check order
open_points.text: A01 says a repeat makes “No other check of stage (6) ... again” and may answer a project whose customer is now restricted, while A04 says “Only an action that passes all six may be a repeat that changes nothing.”
open_points.question: Must a create replay pass all current lifecycle and eligibility checks, or only the reduced checks stated by A01?
options: Apply A01’s reduced replay checks
Require all six A04 stages
Define separate check orders for create replays and repeated transitions
open_points.default_guess: Treat A01 as the specific exception and apply its reduced replay checks.

open_points.subject: Owner-interface CSRF checks
open_points.text: A04 applies to “Every operation — read or change” and places the owner’s CSRF value in stage (1), while A13 says “Every change in the owner interface carries the CSRF protection.”
open_points.question: Must owner-interface reads carry and pass CSRF protection, or only state-changing requests?
options: Require CSRF only for changes
Require CSRF for reads and changes
open_points.default_guess: Require CSRF only for state-changing requests.

open_points.subject: Withdraw pointer project selection
open_points.text: A10 says “An operation on a project that names none uses the session’s active project,” while A08 says “A withdrawal names the pointer only; its project is the pointer’s own.”
open_points.question: For a Kernel withdrawal, is authorization checked against the pointer’s project regardless of the active project, or must the pointer’s project also be active when no project id is supplied?
options: Use the pointer’s own project
Use the active project
Require an explicit project id
open_points.default_guess: Use the pointer’s own project and require only that it be in the granted set.

open_points.subject: Ended agent-session identity reuse
open_points.text: A11 says Kernel uses an identity “it never uses again,” but Registry removes the record and explicitly accepts that registering an ended identity “makes a new session with an empty set.”
open_points.question: How are old audit entries naming the identity distinguished from a newly registered session with that same identity, and must Registry enforce non-reuse?
options: Keep a tombstone and refuse reuse
Allow reuse and add an incarnation identity
Trust Kernel and accept ambiguous history
open_points.default_guess: Keep a non-secret tombstone and refuse reuse.

open_points.subject: Owner-session cookie transport
open_points.text: A13 says the cookie is “sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine,” while A17 allows no configuration item that tells Registry whether its externally visible origin is HTTPS or whether a request came through trusted TLS termination.
open_points.question: How does Registry decide whether to issue a Secure cookie while still supporting any permitted local HTTP access?
options: Always set Secure and require HTTPS everywhere
Derive it from a specified trusted proxy signal
Define separate fixed local and remote cookie behavior
open_points.default_guess: Set Secure unconditionally and require HTTPS for every owner-interface session.

open_points.subject: Owner-session cookie scope
open_points.text: A13 specifies a cookie “that scripts cannot read” and is sent “only to Registry’s own origin,” but gives no SameSite policy, host/domain scope or path scope.
open_points.question: What exact cookie attributes prevent the session from being sent in cross-site or sibling-host contexts?
options: Host-only, Path=/, SameSite=Strict
Host-only, Path=/, SameSite=Lax
Rely only on CSRF protection and browser defaults
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only Secure HttpOnly cookie with Path=/ and SameSite=Strict.

open_points.subject: Concurrent confirmation submissions
open_points.text: A13 says a confirmation value is “used up by the first submission” after session and CSRF checks, but does not say that checking and consuming it are one atomic operation.
open_points.question: Can two concurrent submissions both pass the one-time-value check and execute, or must consumption be atomically won by exactly one submission?
options: Atomically consume before action checks
Serialize all requests in an owner session
Permit both to proceed and rely on later checks
open_points.default_guess: Atomically consume the confirmation value before any subsequent action checks.

open_points.subject: Audit sequence numbers after restore
open_points.text: A15 says “Sequence numbers are never reused,” then says entries lost after restoration “exist nowhere, and their numbers are issued again for new entries.”
open_points.question: Is non-reuse scoped only to the restored history, or must a number ever issued by production remain globally retired even after restoring an older backup?
options: Permit reuse relative to restored history
Persist a sequence watermark outside backups
Refuse restoration that would reuse numbers
open_points.default_guess: Permit reuse and define uniqueness only within the current restored store history.

open_points.subject: Backup encryption
open_points.text: A18 requires that each backup be encrypted and records “a digest of the key,” but specifies no authenticated-encryption scheme, nonce handling, key interpretation, file authentication or digest algorithm.
open_points.question: What exact cryptographic format must implementations use so encryption, tamper detection and key identification are interoperable and testable?
options: Declare one versioned authenticated-encryption format
Leave each backend to choose its own format
Use the store engine’s native encrypted-backup format
open_points.default_guess: Declare a versioned authenticated-encryption format with random nonces and a cryptographic key identifier.

open_points.subject: Backup run during restore reconciliation
open_points.text: A18 says a missed daily backup is made “when it next starts,” while rule 10 says the restored instance is first started owner-only so resurrected erasures and restrictions can be reapplied before service tokens are configured.
open_points.question: If the restored owner-only start occurs after 03:00 UTC, must Registry back up the unreconciled restored state and thereby create a fresh 30-day copy of data that should remain erased?
options: Suppress backups until reconciliation is explicitly completed
Run the backup immediately even before reconciliation
Reconcile offline before Registry starts
open_points.default_guess: Require reconciliation before the process starts or suppress backup runs in an explicit restore-reconciliation mode.

open_points.subject: Post-restore reconciliation completion
open_points.text: A18 requires the owner to reconcile restored data “before configuring the tokens and starting it again,” but also says Registry “cannot list them, enforce them or tell when this is done.”
open_points.question: What prevents service access from being enabled before the required erasures, restrictions and audit-date erasure have actually been restored?
options: Accept an unverifiable manual runbook
Require an explicit recorded reconciliation-complete act
Keep service mode disabled until externally attested
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit durable reconciliation-complete act before service tokens may be enabled.

open_points.subject: Caller values in backend queries and commands
open_points.text: A19 says “No value a caller gives ever becomes part of a query’s or a command’s structure; how the store’s backend lowers this is the backend’s.”
open_points.question: Which backend lowerings satisfy this rule—for example escaped interpolation, query-builder literals, dynamic identifiers, regular expressions, paths or command arguments—and how can the invariant be verified without requiring bound parameters?
options: Require backend-native value binding or an equivalent typed value channel
Allow escaped interpolation certified by the backend
Specify allowed lowering separately for each backend
open_points.default_guess: Require backend-native parameter/value binding and prohibit caller-controlled identifiers, operators and command structure.

open_points.subject: Injection security-review claim
open_points.text: A21 defines the injection category as “no input becomes query, command, template or other interpreted structure,” but the changed A19 rule covers only a caller value becoming query or command structure, plus stored-value rendering and import execution.
open_points.question: What rules prevent caller input from becoming other interpreted structures not covered by those clauses, and does A21 remain complete after the A19 change?
options: Broaden A19 to every interpreted structure
Narrow A21’s claimed category outcome
Add rules for each remaining interpreter boundary
open_points.default_guess: Broaden the normative rule to every interpreter boundary and enumerate the permitted typed-value channels.

open_points.subject: Concurrency security-review coverage
open_points.text: A21 says the concurrency category covers “single-use values, atomic transitions, duplicate submissions” but references only A01, A04, A07, A12 and A14, omitting A13’s one-time confirmation values and A16’s import confirmation and transaction.
open_points.question: Are confirmation consumption and concurrent import submissions within the reviewed concurrency scope, and which accepted decisions prove their behavior?
options: Include A13 and A16 and add their missing concurrency rules
Explicitly exclude owner-session and import concurrency
Treat A04 atomicity as covering both
open_points.default_guess: Include A13 and A16 and require atomic consumption and serialization explicitly.

open_points.subject: Service-token abuse review
open_points.text: A21 says authentication_credential_abuse answers “token lifecycle ... replay, who owns the abuse controls” through A09, A13 and A17, but those decisions provide no behavior for repeated wrong service tokens or replay of a copied valid service token.
open_points.question: Are service-token guessing and bearer-token replay intentionally accepted risks, rate-limited, or assigned to an external control, and how is a compromised token revoked?
options: Declare bearer replay accepted and rotation-at-restart the only revocation
Add Registry-side throttling and token identifiers
Assign detection and blocking explicitly to infrastructure
open_points.default_guess: Declare service tokens bearer credentials, assign abuse monitoring to infrastructure, and specify restart-based rotation as their revocation mechanism.
